title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 (Corvinus): our sentence overturns religion's foundation two ways — precise election without obedience-intuit loves men more than justice and kills all religious solicitude
latin: Hoc posito conantur ostendere sententiam nostram hoc fundamentum religionis duplici modo evertere. Primo, quia statuit Deum sine ullius obedientiae intuitu aliquos praecise ad salutem elegisse: unde sequitur, Deum illos homines magis amasse quam justitiam suam: Quo posito, tollitur obedientiae praestandae necessitas omnisque de religione solicitudo.
pass_a: This being posited they strive to show that our sentence overturns this foundation of religion in a twofold manner. First, because it establishes that God without the intuit of any obedience has precisely elected some unto salvation: whence it follows that God has loved those men more than his own justice: Which being posited, the necessity of rendering obedience is taken away, and all solicitude concerning religion.
pass_b: That assumed, they try to show our view overturns religion's foundation in two ways. First: it sets God as having precisely elected some to salvation without any gaze upon obedience — from which it follows that God loved those men more than his own justice. That granted, the necessity of rendering obedience is taken away, and all care about religion.

lemmas.gloss: Corvinus: our view overturns religion's foundation
election without obedience-gaze loves men over justice

title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 (Corvinus): second way — reprobation to damnation without gaze on disobedience hates the creature without justice-love and kills hope in God
latin: Secundo, quia (ut illi aiunt) statuit Deus aliquos homines ad damnationem praedestinasse sine intuitu inobedientiae: unde rursus sequitur, Deum creaturam suam odisse citra nullam ex amore erga justitiam necessitatem: Quo posito, tollitur spes in Deum. Qui enim certe sibi persuadet se a salute citra peccati intuitum esse reprobatum, credet nihil sibi posse prodesse, quomodocunque studeat peccatum vitare.
pass_a: Secondly, because (as they say) it establishes that God has predestined some men unto damnation without the intuit of disobedience: whence again it follows that God hates his creature apart from any necessity from love toward justice: Which being posited, hope in God is taken away. For he who certainly persuades himself that he has been reprobated from salvation apart from the intuit of sin will believe that nothing can profit him, howsoever he strive to avoid sin.
pass_b: Second: as they say, it sets God as having predestined some men to damnation without any gaze on disobedience — from which again it follows that God hates his creature with no necessity arising from love of justice. That granted, hope in God is taken away. For whoever is sure he has been reprobated from salvation apart from any gaze on sin will believe nothing can profit him, however hard he strives to avoid sin.

lemmas.gloss: kills hope: nothing profits the reprobate

title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 (Corvinus): both inconveniences charged because we teach precise will to save before satisfaction in Christ / faith-foresight, and will to damn apart from impenitence
latin: Utrumque hoc incommodum ex nostra sententia sequi contendunt, quia docemus, Deum quosdam peccatores ita amasse, ut praecise eos voluerit servare, antequam amori suo erga justitiam satisfecerit in Christo, aut eos ut in Christum credentes sit intuitus; atque e contra, Deum quosdam peccatores velle damnare citra considerationem impoenitentiae, licet justitiae suae in Christo Deus satisfecerit.
pass_a: They contend that either inconvenience follows from our sentence, because we teach that God so loved certain sinners that he precisely willed to save them, before he satisfied his love toward justice in Christ, or looked upon them as believing in Christ; and on the contrary, that God wills to damn certain sinners apart from consideration of impenitence, although God has satisfied his justice in Christ.
pass_b: They contend that both inconveniences follow from our view. Why? Because we teach that God so loved certain sinners that he precisely willed to save them before he satisfied his love of justice in Christ, or before he looked on them as believing in Christ. And on the other side, we teach that God wills to damn certain sinners apart from considering impenitence — even though he has satisfied his justice in Christ.

lemmas.gloss: precise will to save before Christ-satisfaction
will to damn apart from impenitence

title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: grave charge — if our sentence uproots Christianity's foundations it must itself be uprooted; we grant their double-love foundation but deny our sentence fights it
latin: Grave profecto hoc crimen est quod nobis objicitur. Nam si sententia nostra convellat religionis Christianae fundamenta, est ipsa quidem ab imis fundamentis revellenda. Expendamus igitur quam vera sit haec criminatio. Atque inprimis non intendimus ullam litem adversariis de duplici illo amore in quo religionis fundamentum collocant; sed negamus sententiam nostram huic amori repugnare.
pass_a: Truly this crime which is objected unto us is grave. For if our sentence uproots the foundations of the Christian religion, it is itself indeed to be torn up from the lowest foundations. Let us therefore weigh how true this accusation is. And first we intend no quarrel with the adversaries concerning that twofold love in which they place the foundation of religion; but we deny that our sentence fights against this love.
pass_b: Truly this charge against us is grave. If our view uproots Christianity's foundations, it must itself be torn up from the roots. So let us weigh how true the accusation is. First: we pick no quarrel with the adversaries over that twofold love in which they set religion's foundation — but we deny that our view fights that love.

lemmas.gloss: if it uproots Christianity, uproot it

title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: two alleged inconveniences of precise election without obedience-gaze — loves predestined more than justice; kills necessity of faith, obedience, and religious care
latin: Instant, nos statuere Deum sine ullius obedientiae intuitu aliquos praecise ad salutem elegisse: Quam opinionem duobus incommodis urgeri arbitrantur. Unum est, quod ponat Deum taliter praedestinatos magis amare quam justitiam suam, quia vult eos servare, antequam amori suo erga justitiam satisfecerit in Christo, aut eos ut in Christo credentes praeviderit. Alterum est, quod tollat omnem necessitatem fidei et obedientiae, omnemque religionis solicitudinem, quia dicimus taliter praedestinatos amari a Deo ad salutem ante et citra praevisionem fidei et obedientiae in iisdem.
pass_a: They press that we establish that God without the intuit of any obedience has precisely elected some unto salvation: Which opinion they judge to be urged with two inconveniences. One is, that it places God as loving those so predestined more than his own justice, because he wills to save them before he has satisfied his love toward justice in Christ, or has foreseen them as believing in Christ. The other is, that it takes away all necessity of faith and of obedience, and all solicitude of religion, because we say that those so predestined are loved by God unto salvation before and apart from foresight of faith and of obedience in the same.
pass_b: They press that we set God as having precisely elected some to salvation without any gaze on obedience. That opinion, they think, is pressed by two inconveniences. One: it makes God love those so predestined more than his own justice, because he wills to save them before he has satisfied his love of justice in Christ, or foresaw them as believing in Christ. The other: it takes away all need of faith and obedience, and all care for religion, because we say those so predestined are loved by God unto salvation before and apart from foresight of faith and obedience in them.

lemmas.gloss: two inconveniences alleged against precise election
loved to salvation before/apart from faith-foresight

title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: difference from Arminius — not that elect can be saved while remaining unbelieving, but that faith/obedience is not antecedent election-motive from free will determining itself
latin: Respondeo: Non in eo situm est discrimen sententiae nostrae ab Arminiana, quod ille electos non posse salvari statuat absque praestita fidei et obedientiae conditione, nos autem opinemur eos servari posse etiamsi maneant infideles et Deo rebelles: sed quod ille hanc fidei et obedientiae conditionem facit antecedaneum electionis motivum, et hunc actum credendi suspendit a libero arbitrio per gratiam Dei excitato et quasi ad aequilibrium quoddam reducto, sed seipsum ante electionem determinante, et inde electionem Divinam procurante.
pass_a: I answer: The discrimination of our sentence from the Arminian is not situated in this, that he establishes that the elect cannot be saved without the condition of faith and of obedience having been rendered, but we opine that they can be saved even if they remain unbelieving and rebellious unto God: but that he makes this condition of faith and of obedience an antecedent motive of election, and suspends this act of believing from free choice excited by the grace of God and as it were reduced unto a certain equilibrium, but determining itself before election, and thence procuring the Divine election.
pass_b: I answer: Our view does not differ from the Arminian in this — that he holds the elect cannot be saved without faith and obedience rendered, while we think they can be saved even if they stay unbelieving and rebellious to God. The difference is this: he makes that condition of faith and obedience an antecedent motive of election, and hangs the act of believing on free choice excited by God's grace and as it were brought to a certain balance, yet determining itself before election and thereby procuring divine election.

lemmas.gloss: we do not allow salvation while remaining unbelieving

title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: we judge faith/obedience necessary to eternal life by fixed decree — yet as special gift prepared in predestination, produced by special operation, foreseen as medium not motive
latin: Nos e contra, quamvis fidei et obedientiae conditionem (si de adultis loquamur) ad vitam aeternam consequendam, ex Dei fixo decreto plane necessariam judicemus, tamen agnoscimus hanc fidem et obedientiam non praevisam fuisse in hac aut illa singulari persona, tanquam ex libero ejus arbitrio per gratiam communem excitato enascentem, et electionis beneficium post se trahentem; sed tanquam speciale donum fuisse huic et illi singulari personae in decreto praedestinationis ab aeterno praeparatum, et ex humana voluntate speciali quadam operatione ab eodem decreto dependente producendam, et inde ab aeterno praevisam in omnibus electis, non tanquam motivum quo ipsi consequantur suam electionem, sed tanquam medium quo praecedente consequentur regnum caelorum ad quod fuerunt electi.
pass_a: We on the contrary, although we judge the condition of faith and of obedience (if we speak of adults) plainly necessary unto obtaining everlasting life from the fixed decree of God, yet we acknowledge that this faith and obedience was not foreseen in this or that singular person as springing from his free choice excited by common grace, and dragging after itself the benefit of election; but as a special gift prepared from eternity for this and that singular person in the decree of predestination, and to be produced from the human will by a certain special operation depending from the same decree, and thence foreseen from eternity in all the elect, not as a motive by which they themselves obtain their election, but as a medium by which preceding they will obtain the kingdom of the heavens unto which they were elected.
pass_b: We take the other side. For adults we judge faith and obedience plainly necessary to everlasting life by God's fixed decree. Yet we deny that this faith and obedience was foreseen in this or that person as something springing from free choice stirred by common grace, and then dragging election's benefit after it. We hold instead that it was a special gift, prepared from eternity for each elect person in the predestination decree. It is to be produced from the human will by a special operation that depends on that decree. From eternity, then, it was foreseen in all the elect — not as the motive by which they win their election, but as the preceding medium by which they reach the kingdom of heaven to which they were elect.

lemmas.gloss: faith as prepared gift, not free-will election-motive
foresight of faith as medium, not motive of election

title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: first inconvenience fails — electing Peter/Paul to infallible share of Christ before foreseeing free will inclined is supreme love of justice, not loving them more than justice
latin: Hoc praemisso, sententia nostra praedictis duobus incommodis haud implicatur. Non priore; Quia Deus non arguitur magis amasse Petrum aut Paulum quam suam justitiam, si illos ab aeterno elegit et designavit ad infallibilem participationem Christi, fidei, et salutis, antequam praevidit liberum illorum arbitrium per oblationem gratiae sufficientis ad Christum amplexandum, fidem concipiendam, salutisque viam capiessendam, efficaciter et perseveranter inclinatum. Imo hoc arguit summum amorem justitiae in Deo, quod Petrum et Paulum, quos ad salutem ex mera misericordia eximie dilexit, noluerit tamen ad hanc salutem illis destinatam perducere nisi talibus mediis adhibitis quibus justitiae suae prius satisfaceret.
pass_a: This being premised, our sentence is by no means implicated in the aforesaid two inconveniences. Not in the former; Because God is not argued to have loved Peter or Paul more than his own justice, if from eternity he elected and designated them unto the infallible participation of Christ, of faith, and of salvation, before he foresaw their free choice efficaciously and perseveringly inclined through the offer of sufficient grace unto embracing Christ, conceiving faith, and taking the way of salvation. Nay, this argues the supreme love of justice in God, that Peter and Paul, whom of mere mercy he exceedingly loved unto salvation, he yet would not lead unto this salvation destined for them unless such means were applied by which his justice would first be satisfied.
pass_b: That premised, our view is not caught in those two inconveniences. Not the first: God is not charged with loving Peter or Paul more than his own justice if from eternity he elected and designated them to infallible share in Christ, faith, and salvation before he foresaw their free choice efficaciously and perseveringly inclined — through the offer of sufficient grace — to embrace Christ, conceive faith, and take the way of salvation. Nay, this argues supreme love of justice in God: that Peter and Paul, whom of mere mercy he loved exceedingly unto salvation, he yet would not lead to that destined salvation unless such means were used by which his justice would first be satisfied.

lemmas.lemma: non ... magis amasse ... quam suam justitiam
lemmas.gloss: electing before free-will-foresight ≠ love men over justice
salvation only by means that first satisfy justice
